title: Semver charter and staged-breaking taxonomy with LTS branching playbook
creator: Ananya Gupta
description: This ticket codifies a runtime-focused semantic versioning charter with a staged breaking-change taxonomy, LTS branching rules, and a prescriptive rollout + upgrade-tooling playbook. The goal is to reduce surprise regressions for hosted and dedicated customers while enabling safe evolution of the serving runtime (kernel selection, KV cache format, RPC schema, model-config contract). This doc ties together: (1) breaking-change classification and required artefacts, (2) deprecation header and minimum notice windows, (3) LTS branch policy and backport criteria, (4) automated upgrade gates (CI/Canary/Observability thresholds), and (5) end-to-end migration tooling we will provide to customers and internal upgrade pipelines.
deprecation_policy_summary: All externally-visible runtime surface changes that remove or alter behavior must include: a deprecation header (X-Redwood-Deprecation: YYYY-MM-DD;reason), a migration guide, and a minimum notice window. Classification: Non-breaking (patch/minor), Soft-breaking (minor-major semantics change requiring opt-in), Hard-breaking (major version and migration required). Minimum windows: Non-breaking 0 days, Soft-breaking 45 days, Hard-breaking 90 days. LTS channel: only security and critical regressions are backported; feature removals never backported.
breaking_change_taxonomy: Class A — ABI/On-disk and KV-cache format changes: always treated as Hard-breaking. Requires compatibility shim or explicit migration path. Example: changing checkpoint KV layout or attention-cache blob layout.

Class B — Public RPC/REST schema changes: Soft-breaking when additive (new optional fields) or Hard-breaking if existing fields change semantics or are removed. Example: changing /v1/generate request shape or removing model_config.max_tokens.

Class C — Behavioral tuning that can change output characteristics (sampling default changes, new kernel fallbacks): treated as Soft-breaking if observable by user features; otherwise Non-breaking with telemetry labeling. Example: default top_p change from 0.95 to 0.92 triggers deprecation header if opt-out not available.
Class D — Internal-only refactors (non-public interfaces): Non-breaking but must pass compatibility smoke tests for Dedicated and Private deployments.
Decision matrix: any change touching Class A or hardening Class B requires a major-version bump and runtime-compatibility gate approval from Release Engineering and APPLIED-ML lead.
lts_branching_guidelines: LTS branches are cut from a release branch marked as stable for 4 weeks of production traffic with SLO adherence. Branch naming: release/x.y-lts, maintenance/x.y. Only the most recent two LTS major versions are actively supported. Backport criteria: (1) security fix, (2) data-loss/regression fix with high customer impact, (3) correctness bug that violates API contract. Feature additions and deprecations are not eligible for backport. Emergency hotfix path available with Security Review and >2 approvers on the patch PR.
rollout_gates_and_metrics: Canary: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over automated 24–72 hour windows depending on change class.

Gate thresholds: latency P50/P95 increase <= 10% from baseline, error-rate (5xx) delta <= 0.1% absolute, quality regressions measured by eval prompts must be within defined regression budget per model.

Automated rollback conditions: breach of latency/error thresholds for >30m, or quality regression > configured budget across canary prompts. Rollback must be executed automatically by the rollout controller and notified to oncall.
Safety net: fallback routing to compatible model variant or previous runtime minor build if degradation occurs.
Observability hooks: trace sampling, token-level cost delta, and new 'compatibility-regression' metric emitted by runtime for each request during canary.
Release approvals: Release Engineering, Runtime Owners, Security (if security_review_required=true), and Product for customer-impacting changes.
upgrade_tooling_and_migration: redwood-compat-check: CI plugin that verifies API schema, kernel ABI signatures, and config file compatibility across candidate builds.

redwood-migrate (CLI): generates a migration plan for on-disk formats, including checksum validation, dry-run mode, and rollback instructions. Supports --kv-cache, --checkpoint, --model-config options.
compat-shim-generator: build-time helper that can emit byte-compatible adapters for limited ABI changes where safe (only allowed for Class B additive cases).
in-console migration assistant: per-customer guided upgrade runbook with preflight checks, impact estimation, and schedule builder for dedicated/private customers.
sample pipeline: GitHub PR -> redwood-compat-check (blocking) -> Canary deployment -> perf/quality gates -> staged-rollout job with auto-rollback enabled.
testing_and_quality_signALS: Mandatory checks for any change touching public contract or binary formats: unit tests, contract tests (contract-test-suite), interoperability test matrix across runtime kernels (CUDA/ROCm/CPU), and a staged-eval against canonical prompt set maintained in evals repo. Signals: contract-test pass, canary perf within gates, no regression on top-100 customer prompts, telemetry sanity checks (cost, tokenization deltas).
communication_and_docs: Change announcement template: include change-class, deprecation window, migration steps, affected APIs, runtime builds, and rollback plan.
Docs to produce for every Soft/Hard breaking change: PRD (short), migration guide, compatibility checklist, and a post-rollout incident review template.
Channels: release-notes (public), internal-release (Slack #rt-release), customer-impact alerts via console and account success team.
acceptance_criteria: Policy text reviewed and approved by Release Engineering, Runtime Owners, and Product.
redwood-compat-check prototype integrated into main CI and running on the release branch.
Migration CLI alpha available and tested on one real internal migration (kv-cache format change example).
Canary gating automation configured for release controller with thresholds codified as defaults.
